description: Figures a household's 2026 estimated tax position from its expected 2026 income, its 2025 tax and what it has withheld and paid: the 2026 tax Form 2210 uses, the safe-harbor required annual payment (the smaller of 90% of the 2026 tax and 100% or 110% of the 2025 tax) and the required amount per installment, the four 2026 due dates, the underpayment and penalty by installment for the payments as given (with their payment dates), and, when the January installment is still open, the amount still due and the penalty if it is paid as the January 15 estimate, withheld in December instead, or not paid. Computed by QuantCalc's federal tax API (Form 2210), the engine the website's estimated tax and underpayment penalty calculators are checked against. Requires a connected QuantCalc PRO licence or Tax Season Pass; without one it returns no figures and names the free calculator. Not tax advice.

age.description: The age the filer reaches in 2026 (18-120).

estimated_payment_dates.description: The date each estimated payment was made (YYYY-MM-DD), in the same order; null for one paid on its due date. A late payment accrues the penalty to the day. Default: every payment on its due date.

estimated_payments.description: The 2026 estimated payments in installment order (April 15, June 15, September 15, January 15). With fewer than four, the January installment is the open one: the result gives what is still due and the penalty three ways (paid as the January estimate, withheld in December instead, nothing more). Default: none.

federal_withholding.description: Federal income tax withheld for all of 2026, including withholding still to come (counted as paid in four equal parts on the due dates). Default 0.

filing_status.description: 2026 filing status: single, married filing jointly (mfj), married filing separately (mfs) or head of household (hoh).

ira_distributions.description: Expected taxable 2026 IRA and 401(k) withdrawals. Default 0.

long_term_gains.description: Expected 2026 net long-term capital gain, negative for a loss. Default 0.

ordinary_dividends.description: Expected 2026 ordinary dividends (Form 1099-DIV box 1a), including the qualified part. Default: the qualified dividends given, else 0.

pension.description: Expected taxable 2026 pension and annuity income. Default 0.

prior_year_agi.description: 2025 adjusted gross income: above $150,000 ($75,000 married filing separately) the prior-year safe harbor is 110% of the 2025 tax. Default: not above it, stated in the result.

prior_year_tax.description: The total tax on the 2025 return (Form 1040 line 24): sets the prior-year safe harbor.

qualified_dividends.description: The qualified part of the dividends, taxed at the capital-gains rates. Default 0.

short_term_gains.description: Expected 2026 net short-term capital gain, negative for a loss. Default 0.

social_security.description: Expected gross 2026 Social Security benefits; the engine figures the taxable part. Default 0.

spouse_age.description: Joint return only: the age the spouse reaches in 2026. Default: the same as age, stated in the result.

tax_year.description: 2026 (default; the only year this tool figures). 2027 is refused, with the reason: 2027 estimated payments need the 2026 return's tax for the prior-year safe harbor (it is filed in 2027) and the IRS's 2027 underpayment interest rates for the Form 2210 penalty, which are not set yet (the rate for January-March 2027 is announced in late 2026). The 2027 tax itself is available now: calculate_2026_income_tax with tax_year 2027.

wages.description: Expected 2026 wages (Form W-2 box 1), the household's total. Default 0.

name: estimated_tax_payments_2026
title: 2026 estimated tax: safe harbor, due dates and Form 2210 penalty
